extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, corporate legal/compliance teams, and securities disclosure professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for preparing climate-related disclosures in Commission filings, including what is baseline disclosure, applicable existing rules and accounting standards, scope and methodology for GHG quantification, and considerations about data quality, timeliness, and comparability across jurisdictions and frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline for measuring benefits and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The baseline includes both the required disclosure of material information under Commission regulation, as well as requirements under other laws that may apply to registrants, and current market practices which may include voluntary disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission treats current disclosure practices (required and voluntary) and other applicable legal requirements as the baseline against which benefits and costs of the final rules are measured. Do not assume the baseline presumes all climate-related information is material; the baseline is descriptive of current disclosure practices and legal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality standard for climate-related information
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must disclose material information about climate-related matters under Commission regulation; the rules do not presume that anything climate-related is per se material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the Commission's usual materiality principles when determining whether climate-related information must be disclosed. The Commission explicitly disagreed with the suggestion that the baseline implies that everything climate-related should be presumed material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of existing SEC rules (Regulation S-K and S-X and 2010 Guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing rules, primarily Regulation S-K and Regulation S-X, and the SEC's 2010 Climate Guidance describe how climate change issues may already be required to be disclosed under current rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult section III of the 2010 Guidance and relevant Regulation S-K/S-X items when determining what climate-related information is already required to be included in filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 101 / historical Item 101(c)(1)(xii) disclosure expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically Item 101 required disclosure 'as to the material effects that compliance with Federal, state and local provisions... relating to the protection of the environment, may have upon the capital expenditures, earnings and competitive position of the registrant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should disclose material estimated capital expenditures for environmental controls and related material effects for current and succeeding fiscal years where material, consistent with the historical scope of Item 101 and related updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Factors / Item 105 disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk Factors disclosure (formerly Item 503(c), moved to Item 105 in 2019) should include material climate-related risks where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that climate-related risks are captured in the risk factors section as appropriate under Item 105, reflecting regulatory renumbering and current expectations for risk disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statement implications and accounting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must consider any financial statement implications of climate-related matters in accordance with applicable accounting standards, including FASB ASC Topic 450 (Contingencies) and FASB ASC Topic 275 (Risks and Uncertainties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate climate matters for effects on contingencies, estimates, and disclosures required in financial statements and footnotes per applicable GAAP standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary disclosure obligations (Securities Act Rule 408 and Exchange Act Rule 12b-20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Securities Act Rule 408 and Exchange Act Rule 12b-20 require a registrant to disclose, in addition to expressly-required information, 'such further material information, if any, as may be necessary to make the required statements... not misleading.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prescribed disclosure items would be misleading without additional climate-related information, include the additional material information to avoid misleading statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHGRP coverage limitations and comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA's Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) does not include emissions from agriculture, land use, or direct emissions from sources with annual emissions <25,000 metric tons CO2e; it does not cover Scope 2 electricity-purchase emissions and represents facility-level data for large direct emitters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on or referencing GHGRP data, disclose its coverage limitations: GHGRP direct-emitter data covers about half of U.S. emissions, and including suppliers increases coverage to ~85–90%. Recognize these limits when assessing completeness and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of direct emitters vs suppliers and Scope 2 treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA defines 'direct emitters' as facilities that combust fuels or otherwise put GHGs into the atmosphere directly; 'suppliers' supply products that when combusted/released generate emissions. The GHGRP does not include reporting of data on electricity purchases or indirect emissions from energy consumption (Scope 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about which scopes and entity categories (direct emitters, suppliers) are included in disclosures, and clarify treatment of Scope 2 emissions when referencing EPA or other datasets that exclude them.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG quantification standards and methodology disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: In the U.S. and other jurisdictions, GHG emissions quantification and reporting are generally based on the widely-used GHG Protocol, though other standards (e.g., ISO) exist and the SEC recognizes those differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose the specific protocol or standard used to quantify emissions and any methodological choices or deviations; explain which gases are included and reconcile differences with other datasets or standards where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of gases and definitional differences across programs
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA requires reporting on some gases (e.g., certain fluorinated ethers) that are optional under the GHG Protocol and that are not included within these final rules' definition of 'greenhouse gases.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which greenhouse gases are covered by the registrant's disclosures and note any divergences from GHGRP, GHG Protocol, or other frameworks; explain implications for comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and alignment with external frameworks (TCFD, ISSB, SASB, ESRS/CSRD)
rubrics_metrics.description: The TCFD recommendations have been incorporated into ISSB standards (TCFD fulfilled its remit and transferred tracking responsibility to ISSB). Other jurisdictional frameworks (e.g., EU CSRD/ESRS) exist and may overlap or differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether disclosures follow TCFD/ISSB/SASB/ESRS/CSRD conventions, explain any alignments or deviations, and recognize that jurisdictions may implement TCFD-aligned requirements differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability under EU CSRD and 'large' company definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For CSRD purposes, a 'large' company meets at least two of the following: balance sheet total > €25 million; net turnover > €50 million; more than 250 employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess CSRD applicability using the CSRD size criteria and other CSRD conditions (e.g., EU-regulated market listing) when determining overlap or comparative obligations for multinational registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining applicability based on listing status and other jurisdictional triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: CSRD first stage is specific to companies trading on an 'EU-regulated market' (a defined term under EU securities law); listing status may be one condition among others for required disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on listing status to determine applicability; consider fiscal-year, turnover attributable to the EU, and other CSRD conditions when determining whether EU rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of emissions disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures of Scope 1 and 2 emissions are often delayed (registrants disclosed with a one- to two-year delay; GHG emissions disclosures can be 12–18 months out of date when published).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to minimize lag between reporting period and publication; disclose reporting periods and any delays clearly, as stale data reduces decision-usefulness for investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure quality: avoid boilerplate and cherry-picking
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical research shows voluntary disclosures often are poor quality and that companies may cherry-pick and report primarily non-material climate information; about 50% of registrants provide generic or boilerplate sustainability information in filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific, decision-useful, non-boilerplate disclosures; avoid selective ('good only') reporting and ensure material climate risks and impacts are not omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-usefulness and investor navigation concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Investors may find it difficult to navigate filings to identify, compare, and analyze climate-related disclosures across filings, and keyword/NLP methods are limited in assessing decision-usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure and label disclosures for comparability and investor usability; supplement automated/topic-keyword methods with substantive narrative and data that convey decision-useful information rather than relying solely on keyword presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of automated text/keyword analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Keyword searches can identify whether a company provides climate-related disclosures but are unable to discern the extent or decision-usefulness of those disclosures; word-embedding NLP is limited in determining decision-usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing filings, supplement keyword/NLP searches with manual review and richer analytic methods to assess the substance and usefulness of disclosure rather than relying solely on superficial text indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching and data linkage practices when using external datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission staff matched GHGRP parent companies to registrants based on company name using Levenshtein Distance and then manually reviewed matches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When combining external emissions datasets with registrant data, document matching methodology, perform manual review to validate matches, and disclose limitations or potential mismatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative compliance pathways under state laws (example: California Climate-Related Financial Risk Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: A company will satisfy California's Climate-Related Financial Risk Act if it prepares a publicly accessible biennial report that includes climate-related financial risk disclosure information by: (1) complying with a law/regulation/listing requirement consistent with the Act's requirements, or (2) voluntarily using a framework that meets the Act's requirements or is in compliance with ISSB standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For registrants subject to multiple regimes, document how a given report or framework satisfies overlapping state or jurisdictional requirements and indicate the method relied upon to meet each applicable obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconcile duplicated/overlapping reporting regimes and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's GHGRP has reporting purposes and authorities distinct from the SEC's proposed rule; some commenters argued that EPA or other jurisdictions' regimes should form the basis of GHG disclosure and that duplicative reporting may be inefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing disclosures that overlap with other regulators' datasets or requirements, explain the purposes and scope differences and clarify why the registrant's disclosures under SEC rules are necessary for investors even where other reporting regimes exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of data sources, third-party vendors, and data accuracy concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Market participants report relying on third-party vendor data (which may include estimates) to assess climate-related metrics; vendors' estimation methodologies can under-estimate actual emissions, and these processes can be inefficient and resource intensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose use of third-party data sources, describe estimation methods and limitations, and where possible validate vendor estimates or supplement with issuer-provided data to improve accuracy and transparency.
